item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J00770","case1_error":"Counts only one of two sandwiches; also evaluates the displayed sum as $30.25 instead of $32.25.","case2_error":"Treats the per-pair price as Monday’s spending, assigns $60 to Tuesday, and ignores the fourfold spending requirement.","reason":"The first omits a purchased unit and misadds; the second confuses per-pair cost with daily spending and replaces the stated daily relationships.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00771","case1_error":"Divides by four siblings instead of five recipients, excluding Jose from the divisor.","case2_error":"No clear error: $140 totals four weekly deposits correctly; the meaning and endpoint of “a month from now” are ambiguous.","reason":"The first uses the wrong recipient count. The second reasonably calculates accumulated savings; the reference instead gives a weekly deposit amount.","judgment":"uncertain"},{"pair_id":"J00772","case1_error":"Uses the initial nine T-shirts as the tripling base instead of the three remaining sweaters, producing negative missing items.","case2_error":"Evaluates 23 + 12 + 17 − 3 − 1 as 40, although the expression equals 48.","reason":"The first chooses the wrong comparison base; the second demonstrably miscalculates its written expression, regardless of ambiguity about overlapping books.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00773","case1_error":"Reduces the required length by 25% instead of accounting for lost usable rope in the purchased supply.","case2_error":"Invents 21 cats for Ben by applying Dave’s cat relationship to Ben as well.","reason":"The first applies a loss adjustment to the wrong side of the requirement; the second assigns an unsupported quantity to another person.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00774","case1_error":"Equates the two remaining patients’ total with the three remaining patients’ total, contradicts x = 6, then doubles an already combined total.","case2_error":"Computes 28 people per week but labels that quantity per day, omitting division by seven.","reason":"The first creates inconsistent subset equations and double-counts a total; the second answers with a weekly quantity instead of the requested daily quantity.","judgment":"different"}]}
